subject: Exec briefing — ROI targets, risks, and procurement path (Helixion Therapeutics)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@helixiontx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap — Helixion exec briefing: outcomes, risks & procurement path

Amelia / Oliver — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Below is a concise recap and the immediate next steps so your execs and procurement team have a single reference. I want to make sure we captured the right priorities; please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you called out:
- Inference latency spikes for the clinical QA assistant during overnight batch updates (95th pct latency ~750ms under peak load).
- Model-cost run-rate is growing fast once traffic scales; current infra budgets exceed planned cost targets for the product launch.
- Regulatory/data residency requirements for PHI-adjacent features in EU and certain US regions.

Stated goals / acceptance criteria from today:
- 95th percentile inference latency < 150ms for interactive queries (target for GA).
- Per-token compute cost reduction of ~30% at target Q4 traffic levels.
- Service availability SLA expectation: 99.95% with on-call escalation.
- Pilot window: 8–12 weeks for functional validation and procurement sign-off.

Proposed business outcomes (what Helixion should see):
- Faster clinician response times (~2x improvement for interactive flows) which maps to ~6% improvement in task throughput for the pilot cohort.
- Estimated 28–35% TCO reduction at scale with a Dedicated + quantized model profile (see attached ROI calc).
- An audit-ready controls package and private deployment options to satisfy the regulatory checklist.

Risks we discussed
- Security: need to confirm SOC 2 and encryption-at-rest for the pilot cluster (we provided SOC 2 attestation during call).
- Quality/regression: model quantization can impact specific prompt behaviors — we will run an A/B eval set you provided.
- Procurement timeline: internal approvals (legal + security) may add 3–4 weeks to the target schedule.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
1) Redwood to provision a 48-hour benchmark run on Redwood Dedicated in us-east-1 (Jonas) — target start: 2027-06-23.
2) Jonas to share the performance/ROI workbook and a draft MSA for internal review (attachments).
3) Helixion to provide security questionnaire and a prioritized eval prompt set by 2027-06-25 (Amelia).
4) Schedule an executive procurement touchpoint to review pilot results and terms — suggested date: 2027-06-30 (all).

Attachments included: Helixion_ROI_calc_Q2.xlsx, Redwood_draft_MSA_v1.pdf

If that aligns, I will: (a) kick off the benchmark provisioning today; (b) route the draft MSA to your legal contact; and (c) set the 6/30 slot on the calendar once you confirm attendee list.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@helixiontx.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@helixiontx.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Helixion exec briefing: outcomes, risks & procurement path

Jonas — thank you, this is very helpful and captured cleanly. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 150ms target is for interactive clinician queries only; batch inference for overnight jobs can tolerate higher latencies but must be cost-efficient.
- Our security lead (Lilah Chen) will own the questionnaire; I will ask her to send the completed document by Friday (6/25).
- For procurement: our legal team prefers to review a redline-ready MSA (if you can provide a Word version we will expedite).

On timeline: the exec procurement touchpoint on 6/30 works for initial sign-off conditioned on the benchmark results. Can you confirm the exact outputs we will present on 6/30 (latency p95, cost delta at scale, and a proposed SLA/cost table)?

Thanks — Amelia

Thanks for the clear recap, Jonas. Quick internal alignment on procurement and coverage: 
- Procurement path (recommended): 1) Pilot SOW and dedicated trial (redwood-managed cluster), 2) Legal review of redline MSA, 3) Procurement PO or reserved capacity contract for Dedicated (if pilot metrics meet thresholds).
- Required artifacts to accelerate approval: a Word copy of the MSA for redlining, SOC 2 report + pen test summary, architecture diagram showing data flow and encryption boundaries, and a short SOW (1–2 pages) that describes trial scope and acceptance criteria.

Action items: 
- Monica will prepare a draft 1-page SOW for the pilot by EOD 6/22 and will include the acceptance criteria Jonas listed.
- Jonas: please add the specific p95/p50 latency numbers and the cost-per-1M-token delta from the benchmark output into the SOW after the 48-hour run.
- Vivek: please prepare the standard enterprise pricing tiers and a high-level escalation path (SRE contact + on-call window) to include in the procurement packet.

I will coordinate with our pricing and legal leads to speed the redline process. Laura

Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

- proposed SLA and escalation path;

I will: provision the trial today, upload the raw perf logs and the ROI workbook to the Drive folder (link above), and share a Word version of the MSA to your legal contact. Monica will route the 1-page SOW draft by tomorrow EOD.

Proposed follow-up calendar: 6/30 11:00–11:45 ET (executive procurement touchpoint). If that works I will send a calendar invite and include a DocuSign link for a preliminary SOW signature if you want to pre-authorize trial provisioning.
